websiteNote: From 4 pages of their campaign website, including its issues section.

Elections and government.summary: Says they would push to make major state contracts and deals public before they are final.
Elections and government.quote: Push for real-time public disclosure of major state contracts, incentive packages, and economic development agreements before they're finalized — not after.

Taxes and spending.summary: Says they would have outside auditors check large state contracts and economic development deals.
Taxes and spending.quote: Independent audits of large state contracts and economic development agreements, not just internal agency sign-off.

Schools and education.summary: Says they oppose school voucher programs, which they say take money from rural and local schools.
Schools and education.quote: Colt opposes school voucher schemes that siphon funding away from rural communities and local schools.

Public safety.summary: Says they oppose the planned 3,000-bed prison in Franklin County.
Public safety.quote: Colt opposes the proposed 3,000-bed prison in Franklin County — a costly, poorly-planned project that will harm rural communities without making Arkansans safer.

Energy and the environment.summary: Says they would push for a state plan to protect power customers and water supplies for families and farms.
Energy and the environment.quote: As governor, he will push for an Arkansas Ratepayer and Water Protection framework that puts Arkansas families and farms first.

Farming and rural life.summary: Says they would support policies that help family farms stay in business across generations.
Farming and rural life.quote: Supporting policies that keep family farms economically viable across generations, not just large agribusiness operations.

Roads and infrastructure.summary: Says they would give rural roads, broadband, and power grids the same attention as those in cities.
Roads and infrastructure.quote: Ensuring rural infrastructure — roads, broadband, and grid reliability — gets the same attention as infrastructure in urban centers.
